title: America/Vancouver noon daily across 2026-11-01 (BC abolished DST in tzdb 2026b)

normative.title: tzdb 2026b (2026-04-22): British Columbia permanent -07
normative.quote: British Columbia's 2026-03-08 spring forward was its last foreseeable clock change, as it moved to permanent -07 thereafter.
normative.note: tzdb models the change at 2026-11-01 02:00 to work around a CLDR limitation, although it legally took place on 2026-03-09

cases.label: tzdb>=2026b
cases.note: Permanent -07; the abbreviation becomes MST and the clock never goes back.

expect.note: A one-hour difference in the absolute firing time of a daily job, caused entirely by which tzdb the process loaded.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: The corpus's proof that engine version is not sufficient provenance. Two runs of the identical library on the identical expression differ by an hour because one process read /usr/share/zoneinfo and the other read a bundled copy. Any conformance claim that does not name a tzdb release is unfalsifiable.

title: America/Edmonton noon daily across 2026-11-01 (Alberta abolished DST in tzdb 2026c)

normative.title: tzdb 2026c (2026-07-08): Alberta permanent -06; Morocco permanent UTC 2026-09-20
normative.quote: Alberta's 2026-03-08 spring forward was its last foreseeable clock change, as it moved to permanent -06 thereafter.

cases.label: tzdb>=2026c
cases.note: Permanent -06, reported with the abbreviation CST.

expect.note: Deliberately paired with TZDB-001: the two provinces changed in DIFFERENT tzdb releases, so a process on 2026b is correct for Vancouver and wrong for Edmonton.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: The pair is a three-way discriminator: a run that gets TZDB-001 right and TZDB-002 wrong is on 2026b exactly; both wrong is <=2026a; both right is >=2026c. The corpus can therefore *infer* an engine's tzdb release from its output, which is what makes tzdb provenance auditable rather than self-reported.

title: Africa/Casablanca: Morocco moves to permanent UTC on 2026-09-20

normative.title: tzdb 2026c (2026-07-08): Alberta permanent -06; Morocco permanent UTC 2026-09-20
normative.quote: Morocco plans to move back to permanent UTC, without daylight saving time transitions, on 2026-09-20 at 02:00.

cases.label: tzdb<=2026b
cases.note: Morocco's pre-2026c model keeps +01 outside Ramadan.

expect.note: A third province of the same problem, on a different continent and in a zone whose rules are also Ramadan-dependent.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: Chosen because Morocco's rule is *predictive*: the tzdb entry encodes a plan, not a fait accompli. A schedule computed today for 2027 can change meaning when the plan does, which is the strongest argument that occurrence materialisation must record its tzdb.

title: RRULE weekly at 12:00 in America/Vancouver across the same boundary
rationale: Shows the provenance dependency is a property of the zone data, not of the expression grammar: the RRULE and cron vectors diverge identically.

title: A gap that exists under one tzdb and not another (America/Vancouver 2027-03-14 02:30)

cases.label: tzdb<=2026a/gap-skip
cases.note: 2027-03-14T02:30 is inside the spring-forward gap and is skipped.

cases.label: tzdb>=2026b
cases.note: No transition exists at all, so the DST policy is not even reached and every day fires.

expect.note: Two policy axes compose: the DST-gap policy is only observable under one of the two tzdb releases.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: The most subtle failure this corpus can express. A test suite that pins the DST policy but not the tzdb will pass or fail depending on when the container image was built, and the failure will look like a scheduling bug.

title: Zone abbreviation is not a stable identifier (Edmonton reports CST at -06:00)

normative.title: IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)
normative.note: tzdb abbreviations are advisory and are neither unique nor stable across releases

normative.title: tzdb 2026c (2026-07-08): Alberta permanent -06; Morocco permanent UTC 2026-09-20

cases.label: tzdb>=2026c
cases.note: Reported as CST — the abbreviation of a zone 1,200 km to the east. Any system that persists 'MST' rather than 'America/Edmonton' is now storing a wrong answer.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: Included to close a specific product question: whether an occurrence record may store an offset or an abbreviation instead of an IANA zone id. It may not, and this vector is the proof.

title: A zone whose historical data changed: Europe/Lisbon 1992

normative.title: IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)
normative.note: historical data is revised between releases; the 1992 Portugal change is stable in modern tzdb

expect.note: Portugal moved from WET to CET on 1992-09-27 at 01:00 UTC, changing the STANDARD offset rather than a DST rule. Noon local stays noon local; the UTC instant moves.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: Distinguishes 'the zone's DST rule changed' from 'the zone's standard offset changed'. Engines that cache a single standard offset per zone fail only on the second kind, and only for historical dates.

title: Unknown zone identifier

normative.title: IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)

expect.note: Engines that silently fall back to UTC or to the process's local zone produce a schedule that is off by the local offset and gives no diagnostic. That is the failure this vector detects.

title: Deprecated zone alias (US/Pacific)

normative.title: IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)
normative.note: backward-compatibility Links are shipped in the 'backward' file and are omitted from some slim/vanguard builds and from some ICU configurations

cases.label: links-absent
cases.note: Builds without the 'backward' file reject the identifier.

apscheduler3@tz2026a.error: ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key US/Pacific'

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

croniter@tz2026a.error: ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key US/Pacific'

croniter[day_or=False]@tz2026a.error: ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key US/Pacific'

cronsim@tz2026a.error: ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key US/Pacific'

fugit@tz2026a.error: ArgumentError: fugit: parse returned nil for "0 12 * * * US/Pacific"

php-cron-expression@tz2026a.error: DateInvalidTimeZoneException: DateTimeZone::__construct(): Unknown or bad timezone (US/Pacific)

rationale: Zone identifiers stored years ago may not resolve in a modern slim tzdb build. This is a migration hazard for any product that persists a zone string, and it is a property of the *build* rather than of the release number.

title: Etc/GMT+5 has a NEGATIVE offset (POSIX sign inversion)

normative.title: IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)
normative.note: the Etc/GMT[+-]N zones follow the POSIX TZ sign convention, which is the opposite of ISO 8601

expect.note: Etc/GMT+5 is UTC-05:00. An engine that maps the identifier to +05:00 is ten hours wrong.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: A documented, normative sign inversion that is nonetheless one of the most common zone-handling defects.
